why: Quote verified verbatim at prompt-caching.md:237, second sentence of a two-sentence line ('Disabling caching is occasionally useful when debugging caching behavior with a specific model or provider. To turn it off, set one of these environment variables to `1`:'), table at :241-245, plus :247 on the managed-settings `env` block. The identifier half of the finding is true — no file we own reads DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING or its four family variants, and the only Nessy-side knob is `extendedPromptCache` (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:134), which the interceptor uses to upgrade or strip a TTL (packages/shared/src/unified-network-interceptor.ts:368 stripPromptCacheTtl, :437 upgradePromptCacheTtl) and never to remove a breakpoint. But the CONSEQUENCE — 'there is no way to disable caching for a model or provider while debugging' — is false, and it is the classic 'unwired identifier, handled one layer up' shape. These are the upstream Claude runtime's own env vars, and we ship that runtime: `strings -a node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude` contains 19 occurrences of DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING — six bare, six each of _HAIKU/_SONNET/_OPUS/_FABLE, plus three of an undocumented _MYTHOS (positive control on the same dump: ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H, 4 hits; an earlier zero-hit run was a false negative from macOS lacking `timeout`). Our Claude backend hands it the whole host environment: buildClaudeSubprocessEnv (packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:236-265) spreads `...process.env` and deletes only the three Bedrock routing vars, and it is the single env builder for that path (only caller getDefaultOptions:276). So `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1` exported before launch reaches the runtime and works today. Nothing downstream re-adds a breakpoint: our interceptor only mutates `ttl` on cache_control objects that already exist (unified-network-interceptor.ts:447-486) and never creates one — its own comment at :324 names the SDK as the producer. The organization half of :247 is wired too: DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING is unlisted in MANAGED_ENV_CLASSIFICATION, and classifyManagedEnvVar (packages/shared/src/config/managed-env.ts:189-191) defaults an unlisted name to 'immediate', so applyManagedEnv writes it into process.env at startup — 'writing here is what carries the block into the Pi subprocess, the Claude subprocess and stdio MCP servers' (managed-env.ts:320-324). Sibling-subsystem check: the Pi runtime does not read these names (grep -rail over node_modules/@earendil-works: 0 hits, with cache_control present in pi-ai as the positive control), and the default product path is the Nessy Gateway's OpenAI-like endpoint, where Anthropic `cache_control` breakpoints do not exist — so on the fork's own default path there is no breakpoint to disable, and on the Claude path the documented variables work. Not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3.
correctedState: The five DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING variables have no reader in Nessy source and no product-level toggle — but they do not need one, and the claimed consequence does not hold. They are the Claude runtime's own variables and we ship that runtime: the bundled `claude` binary reads all five (plus an undocumented _MYTHOS), and buildClaudeSubprocessEnv (packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:236) passes the entire host process.env through, stripping only CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK / AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK / ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL. Exporting DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1 disables caching on the Claude path today, and our interceptor cannot undo it because upgradePromptCacheTtl/stripPromptCacheTtl only rewrite the ttl of cache_control blocks that already exist. The managed-settings route of doc line 247 also works: the name is unclassified, so classifyManagedEnvVar returns 'immediate' and applyManagedEnv writes it into the environment every spawn site inherits. What is genuinely absent is any honouring of these names by the Pi runtime or the Nessy Gateway path — but that path is OpenAI-like and carries no Anthropic cache_control breakpoints, so there is nothing there for the variables to switch off.
